title: helm(private): values schema / templating / init-jobs - improve upgrade/rollback compatibility
author: Evan Brooks
release_notes: Stabilize Helm chart values schema, add templating helpers for nodeAffinity/tolerations, make init jobs idempotent for safe upgrade/rollback; no user-facing API changes expected.
description: Summary: Tighten and extend the Helm chart for redwood-private to improve upgrade/rollback safety, make init hooks idempotent, and add a stable values.schema.json for better validation & automation. Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped and VPC/on-prem environments hit intermittent failures during operator upgrades where init jobs created resources that conflicted on rollbacks. This PR hardens the chart, documents upgrade steps, and adds template helpers for consistent toleration/nodeSelector injection. Changes: 1) Add values.schema.json (v2) with explicit nullable defaults and clear enum values for encryption/psp options to prevent invalid installs via CI. 2) Introduce templates/helpers.tpl with functions for merging nodeAffinity/tolerations across components and for producing stable initJob names (prefix + checksum) to avoid resource collisions on retry/rollback. 3) Refactor templates/init-job.yaml to be idempotent: use server-side apply-friendly annotations, create-if-not-exists semantics (pre-check via command), and avoid hard-coded timestamps. 4) Add conditional hooks for postgres-backup init job: when .Values.postgres.backup.enabled == true the hook runs, otherwise it is skipped; the hook now supports post-upgrade cleanup annotations. 5) Add NOTES.txt guidance for safe upgrade/rollback (kubectl patch examples) and a short upgrade checklist for operators. 6) CI: add helm lint/ct (chart-testing) job to the pipeline and a smoke test that deploys chart to KinD with minimal resources. Compatibility and migration: The values schema is backwards-compatible for typical installs. A small subset of deprecated keys (postgres.initImageTag -> postgres.init.image.tag) are still accepted but emit a warning in NOTES; automated migration snippet included. For customers pinning exact values, recommend running helm get values and comparing against schema before upgrading. Testing: Manual upgrade/rollback tested across three clusters (GKE dev, ESX on-prem lab, Kind CI). Added unit tests for helpers.tpl using helm-unittest to validate templating outputs. CI: all new checks pass on latest run except an intermittent network e2e that was retried and passed on rerun. Rollout plan: Merge to main, stage in release-candidate/beta channel for 48h, then promote to stable. If rollback needed, the idempotent init-jobs and stable naming prevent job duplication; notes include exact kubectl steps. Related: ENG-2150 (upgrade safety), OPS-432 (on-prem install flakiness), SUP-7881 (customer-reported postgres init job collision).

Operators should follow NOTES.txt when upgrading; automated migration script included in repo under charts/redwood-private/migrations/2026-02-10-migrate-postgres-keys.sh.
changelog_entry: chart(redwood-private): stabilize values schema, make init jobs idempotent, add templating helpers for affinity/tolerations, improve upgrade/rollback safety
rollout_instructions: 1) Merge to main. 2) Publish release-candidate to beta channel. 3) Run helm upgrade --install with --atomic to ensure rollback on failure. 4) If rollback runs, follow NOTES.txt: kubectl delete jobs/<init-job>-<suffix> if stuck, then helm rollback <release> <revision>. See migration script for deprecated keys.
